meeting_header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 15:00 UTC (07:00 PT)
Duration: 62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Evan Cho (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Northbridge Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Platform), Dr. Amina Khan (Clinical Data), Ravi Nair (PM)
summary: POC scoping to pick shortlist of open models for a clinical-extraction + triage POC. Focus: multilingual (English/Spanish/Portuguese), clinical domain fidelity, latency <200ms p95 for 512-token responses, and throughput for batch nightly processing. Discussed hosted vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs, telemetry for quality evaluation, and timeline for a 4-week pilot.

transcript:
[15:00:02] Maya Patel: alright everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros?
[15:00:09] Lena Ortiz: hi all, lena here, i head ML at Northbridge, we're trying to pick an open model for a small poc to replace some of our rules for discharge summaries
[15:00:16] Marcus Lee: marcus platform eng, i'll own infra side and network for the POC
[15:00:23] Dr. Amina Khan: hi, aminA khan, clinical data, i'll help validate extraction outputs, sorry my audio is a bit low
[15:00:30] Maya Patel: great, and from redwood, samir will dig into benchmarks and evan for integration?
[15:00:36] Samir Gupta: yep, i'll take the bench plan. high level goals? lena, you mentioned extraction — what are must-haves?
[15:00:45] Lena Ortiz: right so must haves: accurate medication extraction, dosage units, and negation handling. we need at least 0.88 F1 on our gold set for medication spans, and hallucination rate below 3% on clinical facts — that's kinda non negotiable for the pilot
[15:01:05] Ravi Nair: and timeline, we're aiming for a 4 week POC to inform Q1 roadmap, so quick turn around
[15:01:12] Evan Cho: ok noted. also, do you expect realtime latency constraints for triage?
[15:01:18] Dr. Amina Khan: yes, for triage UI we want ~200ms p95 for ~512 tokens ideally, but batch nightly ingest can be higher latency
[15:01:28] Marcus Lee: concurrency wise we'll hit maybe 25 concurrent inference calls during peak business hours, plus batch jobs overnight processing ~20k docs per night
[15:01:40] Speaker 1: mhmm
[15:01:42] Samir Gupta: great, that helps sizing. we'll pick 3 models across the open-model spectrum — a larger high quality 30B-ish float or LLM, a mid-size quantized 13B, and a small fast distilled 7B — try to capture latency/cost/quality tradeoffs
[15:01:56] Lena Ortiz: can you name examples?
[15:02:00] Samir Gupta: for the high end we were thinking — i mean there are models like peregrine-similar or big-open-30b (names fuzzy here), then mid is like ortho-13b-quant, and small is distilled-micro7b, we'll send a proper shortlist in the deck after this call 
[15:02:18] Maya Patel: note: model names in the call are placeholders; we'll provide exact HF or registry refs in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[15:02:24] Marcus Lee: how does dedicated vs hosted impact latency/cost here? we prefer managed but may need VPC for PHI-ish data
[15:02:33] Maya Patel: good question — hosted can be fastest to spin up and cheaper for pilot, but for PHI and compliance most customers pick Redwood Private with a customer VPC and our private control plane. that gives you KMS integration and audit logs. The tradeoff is setup time and day-1 cost
[15:02:51] Lena Ortiz: we need SOC2 and audit logs, also SSO with SAML — is that supported in the Private offering?
[15:02:59] Evan Cho: yes, Private supports SAML SSO, SSO + RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. We'll attach the SOC2 report and a checklist.
[15:03:08] Dr. Amina Khan: also need data residency — at least EU for some patients, but most data is US. any constraint on region selection?
[15:03:16] Samir Gupta: Redwood has multi-region options, but for POC we can run everything in US region; if you need EU residency we can spin up private capacity there — might add lead time
[15:03:27] Maya Patel: switching back to bench plan — Samir, run through suggested metrics and test harness?
[15:03:33] Samir Gupta: sure: we'll run three workloads: 1) extraction accuracy: run on 1k de-id clinical notes (you'll provide 200 sample and we'll bootstrap to 1k with synthetics?), 2) latency micro-bench for 512 token responses (p50/p95/p99), 3) throughput for batch (docs/hr) + cost estimate tokens per doc and cost per 1M tokens. We'll also record memory and GPU utilization to estimate Dedicated capacity needs
[15:03:56] Lena Ortiz: wait, about synthetic expansion — we prefer using real examples, but i can give 200 and we can augment; are synthetic examples going to skew hallucination metrics?
[15:04:07] Samir Gupta: yes they can. we'll flag synthetic vs original in the sheet and weight gold-set metrics accordingly. ideally you share as many real as allowed for evaluation
[15:04:16] Marcus Lee: for the nightly batch: 20k docs, average doc size?
[15:04:20] Dr. Amina Khan: avg 800 tokens, but heavy tails, some reports up to 3k tokens; most of the extraction happens in the first 1k tokens though
[15:04:29] Samir Gupta: good to know — that affects KV cache and memory, and some models degrade at longer contexts; we'll include context truncation tests and see quality vs cost tradeoff
[15:04:40] Lena Ortiz: another important thing: Spanish and Portuguese coverage — many of our clinics have Spanish notes and some partners in Brazil. we need minimal drop off in extraction for es/pt — maybe no more than 6% F1 drop relative to english?
[15:04:53] Maya Patel: ok we'll include multilingual slices in the bench. we'll prioritize languages you provide samples for
[15:04:59] Ravi Nair: what about hallucination detection, do you have tooling for automatic checks?
[15:05:04] Evan Cho: we have a quality harness that runs factuality checks and gives a hallucination score per model on a labeled set; it's not perfect but good for relative comparison
[15:05:13] Speaker 2: hmm
[15:05:15] Samir Gupta: operationally, we'll run the bench against your data in two modes: hosted sandbox (no PHI) to get baselines quickly, and then Private on your VPC for final numbers. That way we can iterate faster without waiting for full infra setup
[15:05:30] Lena Ortiz: that aligns with our preference. can you estimate how long Private spin up takes?
[15:05:35] Maya Patel: typically 2-3 weeks for fully locked Private with KMS and SSO; for a POC we can do a lightweight VPC peering test in 3-5 days if infra is ready
[15:05:45] Marcus Lee: ok we'll try to have the test VPC ready in a week — i'll send the firewall rules and a test endpoint config
[15:05:52] Samir Gupta: noted. on model selection we also need to think quantization and memory. mid-size quantized models often give the best cost/latency balance for 512 tokens with modest quality loss; but for clinical facts the 30B float can be noticeably better on hallucination and rare entity extraction
[15:06:11] Lena Ortiz: is that difference measurable on the 200 examples? we're worried about variance
[15:06:16] Samir Gupta: yes there will be variance; that's why we'll run the 1k test set and compute confidence intervals. also we'll run stress cases — rare medications and negations — as separate slices
[15:06:28] Dr. Amina Khan: please include a few examples of ambiguous abbreviations — those trip up models all the time
[15:06:34] Maya Patel: good call. we'll add an ambiguity slice.
[15:06:37] Ravi Nair: budget — what costs should we plan for the pilot? just a ballpark please
[15:06:42] Evan Cho: for hosted bench runs, expect a few hundred to low thousands dollars depending on model size and number of runs. For Private, there is an onboarding/setup charge plus reserved capacity pricing if you want sustained throughput. we'll share a pricing ballpark in the follow-up
[15:06:57] Speaker 3: cool
[15:07:00] Samir Gupta: deliverables: bench spreadsheet with per-model tabs, latency/cost/quality summary, recommended model for production and suggested deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private). We'll also include runbooks for integration and an eval rubric you can use to sign off
[15:07:13] Lena Ortiz: what do you need from us to get started?
[15:07:17] Maya Patel: three things: 1) sample dataset (200 de-id notes + multilingual), 2) success criteria template (F1 thresholds, acceptable latency/cost), 3) confirmation of infra timeline (VPC readiness)
[15:07:29] Lena Ortiz: i can get those by next week
[15:07:32] Marcus Lee: i'll coordinate VPC and firewall, expect a note from me tomorrow
[15:07:36] Maya Patel: perfect. any blockers?
[15:07:39] Dr. Amina Khan: only that we need a legal review on data transfer even for de-id — expect a slight delay but shouldn't block the initial hosted run
[15:07:49] Samir Gupta: understood. we'll start the hosted bench using synthesized samples while legal signs off on PHI transfer for private runs
[15:07:58] Maya Patel: ok let's recap and list next steps — I'll capture in the follow up note. thanks everyone
[15:08:06] Recording ended
